record.paper_title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics
record.original_question: For one-variable elliptic holomorphic germs with a Cremer fixed point at the origin, are two topological invariants sufficient for complete topological classification: the multiplier f'(0) and the homeomorphism class of the stable set germ K_f at the origin? Equivalently, do those two data completely determine the topological local conjugacy class of a Cremer point?

evidence.quote: (OP3) Are the multiplier and the homeomorphism class of the stable set a complete set of topological invariants for discrete holomorphic local dynamical systems in End(C, O) having a Cremer point at the origin?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in \operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C},0)$ be a germ of a holomorphic map fixing the origin, written as $f(z) = \lambda z + O(z^2)$ with multiplier $\lambda = f'(0)$. Assume $|\lambda|=1$ and $\lambda$ is not a root of unity (so the fixed point is irrationally indifferent), and assume further that $0$ is a Cremer point of $f$, i.e., $f$ is not locally holomorphically linearizable at $0$. Define the stable set germ at the origin by
$$K_f = \{z \in U : f^n(z) \in U \text{ for all } n \geq 0\}$$
considered as a germ at $0$ for any sufficiently small neighborhood $U$ of $0$.

Question: Are the pair $(\lambda, [K_f])$ — the multiplier together with the homeomorphism class of the germ $K_f$ at the origin — a complete set of topological invariants for the local topological conjugacy class of $f$ at the origin?

That is, given two such elliptic holomorphic germs $f, g \in \operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C},0)$ each having a Cremer fixed point at $0$, is it true that $f$ and $g$ are topologically conjugate near $0$ if and only if $f'(0) = g'(0)$ and the germs $K_f$ and $K_g$ are homeomorphic at $0$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this classification problem for Cremer fixed points was found. Recent work on hedgehogs and neutral holomorphic germs (e.g., Pérez-Marco and others, including Stony Brook IMS preprints) continues to study the topology of stable sets near Cremer points, but a complete topological classification by multiplier and stable-set homeomorphism class does not appear to be established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hedgehogs for neutral dissipative germs of holomorphic diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies hedgehogs and stable sets for neutral (Cremer-type) holomorphic germs; the topology of stable sets near Cremer points remains an active area.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research on the topology of stable sets near Cremer points, with no complete classification asserted.

status_evidence.title: Nevanlinna, Siegel, and Cremer
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses criteria distinguishing Siegel and Cremer behavior via Nevanlinna theory but does not provide a topological classification of Cremer germs.
status_evidence.claim: No topological classification of Cremer germs is established in this reference.
